extraFacts.fact: Figures of the sibling hoses in this family, as listed on their own pages: Parker 510C 69 to 224 bar; 518C 90 to 207 bar; 520N and 528N 241 to 345 bar; 53DM 207 bar; 540N 86 to 207 bar; 540P 138 to 190 bar, -10°F to +150°F; 55LT 138 to 207 bar, -40°F to +212°F; 575X 345 bar; 580N 138 to 241 bar; B9 17 bar; R7 up to 210 bar; R8 up to 350 bar.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics product listings (descriptions, specs and size tables) for this family, facts dump 2026-11-18

extraFacts.fact: Hose dash sizes count sixteenths of an inch of hose bore: -3 is 3/16 inch, -4 is 1/4 inch, -5 is 5/16 inch, -6 is 3/8 inch, -8 is 1/2 inch, -10 is 5/8 inch, -12 is 3/4 inch and -16 is 1 inch.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 / SAE J514 dash size convention; the Parker 56 Series size tables on this site

extraFacts.fact: SAE J517 gives the general, dimensional and performance specifications for the SAE 100R series of hydraulic hose, including 100R7 (single-fibre-braid thermoplastic) and 100R8 (double-fibre-braid thermoplastic).

faqs.q: What is the Parker 510C Series thermoplastic hose and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Parker 510C Series is a medium-pressure thermoplastic hydraulic hose from Parker's Parflex division. It is listed in 8 part numbers and the maker states 1,000 to 3,250 psi (69 to 224 bar), by size.

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Parker 510C Series, such as 510C-16?
faqs.a: In 510C-16 the 510C is the series and the number after it is the hose size as a dash number in sixteenths of an inch, so -16 is 1 inch hose. 510C-6-6 repeats the number and appears as a second row of the same size with the same pressure, so quote the full part number.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Parker 510C Series come in?
faqs.a: The Parker 510C Series is listed in 8 part numbers: 510C-16 (69 bar), 510C-6-6 (155 bar), 510C-8 (155 bar), 510C-8-8 (155 bar), 510C-5 (172 bar), 510C-4 (207 bar), 510C-4-4 (207 bar), 510C-3 (224 bar). The Sizes & Part Numbers table lists each with its pressure, and other sizes are quoted on request.

faqs.q: How do I choose the size of Parker 510C hose for my pressure?
faqs.a: Choose the bore from the flow you need and then read the pressure for that size: the 510C rating falls from 224 bar on 510C-3 to 69 bar on 510C-16, so a bigger hose carries less pressure. Never use the figure of a smaller size for a larger one.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of Parker 510C Series hose?
faqs.a: The maker states 1,000 to 3,250 psi (69 to 224 bar) for the 510C Series. By part number: 224 bar on 510C-3, 207 bar on 510C-4, 207 bar on 510C-4-4, 172 bar on 510C-5, 155 bar on 510C-6-6, 155 bar on 510C-8. The working pressure in the size table is the maximum for continuous duty; burst pressure is a test figure, not a working limit.

faqs.q: What is Parker 510C Series hose made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives the material as thermoplastic and no further construction detail, so ask us for the tube and cover materials if the fluid is unusual.

faqs.q: Which standard does Parker 510C Series hose follow?
faqs.a: The listing states no hose standard for the Parker 510C Series; it is a Parflex-division thermoplastic hose. Select by the working pressure in the size table, and ask us if your application calls for a standard such as SAE 100R7 or R8, which our R7 and R8 listings cover.

faqs.q: Which fittings go on Parker 510C Series hose?
faqs.a: The hose takes the end fittings that Parker approves for the 510C Series, and fittings must come from that series because a crimped assembly is rated only as a matched combination. See the [thermoplastic hose fittings guide](/blog/thermoplastic-hose-fittings-guide) and the [hydraulic fittings shelf](/c/hydraulic-fittings).

faqs.q: How do I route and install Parker 510C Series hose?
faqs.a: Route the 510C hose with the bend radius and without twist that thermoplastic hose needs, and keep it away from heat and abrasion. The [hose routing, bend radius and twist guide](/blog/hose-routing-bend-radius-twist) sets out the checks; replace any hose with a kinked or damaged cover.

faqs.q: How does the Parker 510C Series compare with the Parker 518C Series?
faqs.a: The Parker 510C is the standard conductive-construction hose, while the [Parker 518C Series Medium Pressure Thermoplastic Non-conductive Hydraulic Hoses](/p/parker-518c-series-medium-pressure-thermoplastic-non-conductive-hydraulic-hoses) is the non-conductive version in the 518C Series. Choose the 518C where the hose works near live electrical equipment; otherwise the 510C is rated up to 224 bar against 207 bar.

faqs.q: What is R7 thermoplastic hydraulic hose (SAE 100R7) used for?
faqs.a: The R7 thermoplastic hydraulic hose is a lightweight single-fibre-braid hose to SAE 100R7, with a polyamide tube and a polyurethane cover, used as a tighter-bending alternative to rubber R1 1SN hose. It works up to 210 bar at -03 and from -40°C to 93°C.

faqs.q: How do I specify the size of R7 thermoplastic hose?
faqs.a: This listing carries no part-number table, so quote the SAE 100R7 grade and the dash size. The dash number is the hose bore in sixteenths of an inch: -3 is 3/16 inch, -8 is 1/2 inch and -16 is 1 inch, which are the bores of 1/8 inch to 1 inch (DN3 to DN25) the listing gives.

faqs.q: Which bore sizes does R7 thermoplastic hose come in?
faqs.a: The R7 hose is listed in bores from 1/8 inch to 1 inch (DN3 to DN25), with outside diameters of 10 to 32.5 mm from -03 to -16. No size table is shown on this page, so send us the bore and length you need and we will quote.

faqs.q: How do I choose the bore of R7 thermoplastic hydraulic hose?
faqs.a: Choose the bore for the flow you need and read the pressure for that size: the listing gives 210 bar at -03 down to 70 bar at -16, so pressure falls as the bore rises. Also check the minimum bend radius, which is 30 mm at -03 and 200 mm at -16.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of R7 thermoplastic hydraulic hose?
faqs.a: The R7 hose is rated 210 bar at -03, falling to 70 bar at -16, with a minimum burst of 840 bar, a safety factor of 4:1. Take the working pressure for your bore, not the figure for the smallest size, and use fittings rated to match.

faqs.q: What is R7 thermoplastic hydraulic hose made from?
faqs.a: The R7 hose has a polyamide (nylon) tube resistant to hydraulic fluid, one layer of synthetic-fibre braid and a smooth polyurethane cover that resists abrasion and weather. The cover is listed as non-conductive; ask for test data if you need it for work near live equipment.

faqs.q: Which standard does R7 thermoplastic hose conform to?
faqs.a: The R7 hose conforms to SAE 100R7, the single-fibre-braid thermoplastic hose in the SAE 100R series that SAE J517 sets out. The listing states a safety factor of 4:1 and no approval beyond that grade.

faqs.q: Which end fittings suit R7 thermoplastic hose?
faqs.a: The hose takes end fittings of the series made for thermoplastic hose, crimped or reusable, with a termination such as JIC 37°, ORFS, BSP, NPT or metric 24° as you specify. The [thermoplastic hose fittings guide](/blog/thermoplastic-hose-fittings-guide) explains the match, and the [hydraulic fittings shelf](/c/hydraulic-fittings) lists the ends.

faqs.q: How do I route and install R7 thermoplastic hose?
faqs.a: Route the R7 hose with at least the minimum bend radius for its bore and without twist, and keep it clear of heat and abrasion.
